t12-001.title: Operating-system resources and foundational data structures

entries.Process: An operating-system resource boundary with its own address space and lifecycle; process isolation costs more than sharing memory between threads.
entries.Thread: A schedulable execution path within a process that shares process memory and therefore requires synchronization around shared state.
entries.Virtual memory: An address-space abstraction backed by physical pages and possibly storage; page faults and working-set pressure can dominate tail latency.
entries.Page cache: Operating-system memory that caches file-backed data, often making repeated reads faster while competing with application memory.
entries.Blocking I/O: An operation where the caller waits until I/O completes; too many blocked worker threads can limit concurrency.
entries.Readiness-based I/O: An I/O model that notifies an event loop when a descriptor can progress, reducing idle thread use while adding state-machine complexity.
entries.File descriptor: A process-local handle to an open file, socket, or similar resource; descriptor limits can constrain connection-heavy services.
entries.Hash table: A key-to-bucket structure with expected efficient lookup under a suitable hash and load policy; collisions and adversarial keys matter.
entries.Skip list: A layered linked structure supporting expected logarithmic search and ordered traversal with simpler probabilistic balancing.
entries.Bloom filter: A compact approximate set-membership structure with possible false positives but no false negatives for inserted values under correct use.
entries.B-tree: A balanced page-oriented search tree that supports ordered lookup and range scans with bounded tree height.
entries.LSM tree: A write-optimized storage structure that flushes sorted runs and compacts them later, trading write behavior for read/space amplification.

t12-001.title: Spatial partitioning and geospatial query structures

entries.Geohash: Encodes a location into a hierarchical string cell; nearby points near cell borders may have different prefixes, so neighboring cells must be queried.
entries.Quadtree: Recursively subdivides a two-dimensional region into four cells, adapting spatial resolution to data distribution.
entries.R-tree: Indexes bounding rectangles in a balanced tree for spatial intersection and range queries; overlapping nodes can increase search work.
entries.S2 geometry: Represents spherical geometry using hierarchical cells mapped from a cube projection, supporting global spatial indexing.
entries.H3 grid: Partitions the globe into hierarchical hexagonal cells with pentagonal exceptions, useful for aggregation and neighborhood queries.
entries.Bounding-box candidate search: Finds a coarse set of spatial candidates before a more exact distance or geometry test; it must account for projection and antimeridian behavior.
entries.Spatial hot cell: A geographic partition with unusually high traffic or data density; split, replicate, or adapt query strategy without losing boundary correctness.

entries.CAP theorem: During a network partition, a distributed data system cannot guarantee both linearizable consistency and a successful response from every non-failing side; outside a partition, the theorem does not rank all designs.
entries.PACELC: Extends the partition tradeoff by describing a latency-versus-consistency choice when there is no partition, alongside behavior during partitions.
entries.Read quorum: The number of replicas whose responses are required for a read under a specified replication protocol; it does not by itself define freshness or ordering.
entries.Write quorum: The number of replica acknowledgements required before a write is reported successful under a specified protocol.
entries.Sloppy quorum: Accepts writes from temporary nodes outside the usual replica set during failure, improving availability but requiring later handoff and repair.
entries.Hinted handoff: Temporarily stores a replica's missed update at another node and forwards it when the intended replica returns.
entries.Read repair: Reconciles stale replicas during a read path; it can improve convergence but adds latency and does not replace background repair.

t12-004.title: Architecture evolution, teams, and execution models

entries.Conway's Law: An organization tends to produce system boundaries that reflect communication boundaries; architecture and team design influence one another.
entries.Team topology: How teams are organized around stream-aligned ownership, enabling platforms, complicated subsystems, or temporary collaboration; it affects cognitive load and service boundaries.
entries.Serverless computing: Runs code or managed capabilities without direct server administration, while capacity limits, cold starts, event semantics, and unit economics still require design.
entries.Function as a service (FaaS): Executes bounded functions on demand under a provider runtime; execution duration, concurrency, startup, and state constraints shape use.
entries.Local-first software: Keeps useful data and behavior on the user device and synchronizes later, requiring merge/conflict, privacy, and revocation rules.
entries.Platform engineering: Builds supported internal capabilities and workflows as a product for delivery teams, with adoption and developer outcomes as measures.
entries.Internal developer platform (IDP): A collection of self-service tools and paved paths that standardize common delivery tasks while allowing justified exceptions.

t12-004.title: Resilience experiments, scaling, and operational economics

entries.Chaos engineering: Runs controlled experiments against explicit steady-state hypotheses to learn how a system behaves under faults; it is not random production breakage.
entries.Game day: A rehearsed operational exercise that validates people, runbooks, signals, and system recovery for a scoped scenario.
entries.Autoscaling: Adjusts capacity from measured signals or schedules; startup delay, warm-up, downstream limits, and scale-in safety constrain effectiveness.
entries.Predictive scaling: Adds capacity based on forecast demand, requiring forecast quality and a fallback for unexpected peaks.
entries.Graceful degradation: Preserves core user value by disabling or simplifying lower-priority functions under stress or dependency failure.
entries.Load shedding: Rejects or discards selected work to protect system capacity and critical operations when demand exceeds safe limits.
entries.FinOps: A cross-functional practice that relates cloud spending to business value, accountability, and optimization decisions.
entries.Spot capacity: Lower-cost interruptible compute that may be reclaimed; use only for work that can checkpoint, retry, or tolerate interruption.
entries.Power usage effectiveness (PUE): A facility-energy-to-IT-equipment-energy ratio; it describes data-center overhead but not the full carbon impact of useful work.
entries.Carbon-aware scheduling: Moves deferrable workloads in time or place based on carbon intensity while honoring latency, residency, and capacity constraints.

t12-004.title: Service identity, perimeter threats, and cryptographic lifecycle

entries.OAuth 2.0: An authorization framework for delegated access; the chosen grant and client type determine the threat model and token handling.
entries.OpenID Connect (OIDC): An identity layer on OAuth 2.0 that provides authentication claims and ID-token semantics.
entries.JSON Web Token (JWT): A compact claims representation that may be signed or encrypted; validate issuer, audience, expiry, algorithm policy, and key rotation.
entries.SPIFFE/SPIRE: A workload-identity approach that issues verifiable identities to running workloads and supports short-lived credentials.
entries.Distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) mit: Layered capacity, filtering, rate control, and traffic absorption to reduce availability impact from volumetric or application-level attacks.
entries.Web application firewall (WAF): An HTTP-aware rule layer that blocks or challenges selected traffic patterns; it cannot repair authorization or input-validation flaws.
entries.Key management service (KMS): A managed cryptographic-key lifecycle and access control service; envelope encryption and key rotation policies remain application concerns.
entries.Supply-chain provenance: Evidence of source, build process, and artifact lineage that supports integrity verification and incident response.
entries.Post-quantum cryptography migration: A staged transition to quantum-resistant algorithms where long-lived confidentiality or signature validity requires it; interoperability and crypto agility must be planned.

t12-005.title: Prompt operations, multi-agent coordination, and model economics

entries.Prompt-as-code: Treats prompt templates and structured instructions as reviewed, versioned artifacts with tests, rollout, and rollback.
entries.Red teaming: Probes a system with adversarial inputs and misuse scenarios to find safety and security failures before and after release.
entries.Multi-agent orchestration: Coordinates multiple model-driven workers or specialists; shared state, failure propagation, loops, and budget need explicit limits.
entries.Planner-executor pattern: Separates task decomposition from action execution; validate every proposed action and bound plan depth and retries.
entries.Model routing: Selects a model/provider using task capability, privacy, quality, latency, quota, and cost constraints.
entries.Model cascade: Tries a cheaper or faster model first and escalates selected cases to a stronger model according to an evaluated policy.
entries.Prompt caching: Reuses provider-side processing for repeated prompt prefixes where supported; it does not cache the full semantic answer by itself.
entries.Streaming speech recognition (ASR): Produces partial speech-to-text results while audio arrives, reducing perceived delay but allowing revisions.
entries.Text-to-speech (TTS) streaming: Emits generated speech incrementally so playback can begin before the full output is available.
entries.Model Context Protocol (MCP): Defines a protocol for exposing context and tools to AI applications; client and server trust, authorization, and input validation remain essential.
entries.Multimodal data pipeline: Ingests and transforms text, image, audio, video, or documents while preserving provenance, access policy, and modality-specific evaluation.
